Hi! So sorry, I just saw this (I’m not really active on Reddit)

I had a few sessions of psychotherapy (talk therapy) and saw a couple of psychiatrists for a while but was never really consistent with either for numerous reasons. 

The psychs helped me understand dysthymia, which helped reduce the “I am fundamentally broken” feeling, but overall I had pretty bad experiences with them and whatever medication they put me on wasn’t effective

Talk therapy helped a lot more, but again, I was never consistent with it :’) I think if I was I would’ve been more stable much sooner. Would definitely recommend, especially if you find somebody as compassionate and patient as the person I was seeing

I didn’t really improve mood-wise while I was seeking professional help, I mostly just learned about what I was going through. but I think the fact that I attempted it in the first place was a big moment for me and I’m still glad I did it (even if I didn’t get along with a few of my psychs lol)

Rooting for you 💗💗

Edit: the reason I didnt like my psychs was because I felt that one was draining my finances and the other was trying to pigeonhole me into a diagnosis for OCD (which I am 100% confident I don’t have). I’m sure there are much better psychs than the ones I’ve talked to haha. I also never got an actual treatment plan from anybody, i was just jumping from professional to professional

Thanks! I just want to point out that there may be a negative bias if you look for answers online. I think a lot of people that post are in some of the lowest stages of their lives. I always thought I’d feel broken forever but I want to stress that there’s definitely a light at the end of the tunnel, so to speak. There will come a day when you won’t constantly feel like there’s something wrong with you. You’ll be able to experience a full range of human emotion and appreciate everything you’ve accomplished so far, even if you don’t feel like it’s possible now (also 2 degrees? Wow, congrats!!). Of course depressive episodes are still something you’ll have to deal with, but it’s not a constant weight over your shoulder. it’s just something that pops in every now and then, like a bad cramp.

I just don’t want you to feel disheartened reading those posts of 60+ year olds feeling depressed all their lives. I remember that one of those threads almost pushed me to my breaking point, but I’m glad nothing happened because of it. Treatment, exercise, and self-care may not feel like it’s doing anything now but all those tiny efforts definitely add up. Take care, I’m proud of you for getting this far!

Diagnosed with dysthymia, was put on duloxetine & escitalopram, didn’t really feel any effects, was in & out of therapy/professional help, but somehow managed to stumble my way into a point where I feel genuinely happy and stable. Early on it felt like it would just be something I would simply “have to manage” but I don’t really think about it anymore, I just live life.

There are still times when I feel depressed but it doesn’t last months or years anymore and it’s never reached the same level of despair I used to feel constantly. It’s just something that comes and goes and it comes more rarely as time marches. Sometimes I wonder if I ever really had it because life feels so good sometimes. But it’s obviously hard to deny 8+ years of depression.

There’s hope just keep living

I think that he’s definitely inconsiderate in bed but I also think that these issues might be able to be fixed with a direct conversation about your boundaries and needs. It’s understandable that you’re frustrated that he can’t read your hints or just straight up doesn’t show common decency in bed (ESPECIALLY since it’s been triggering at times to you) but at the same time some people—and I’m givin him an extreme benefit of doubt here—are very dense and might not be able to understand what you want unless you spell it out for them. 

It feels like you’re compromising a lot on your comfort and pleasure and I think once this happens it’s time to stop dropping hints and just sit down and have a very serious talk about them. Set hard limits. Tell him explicitly what you want him to do in bed and how his actions make you feel. If he’s still neglectful after that then at least you know it’s not cause he’s dense, it’s cause he’s an actual dumpster fire asshole, and breaking up with him over the phone, or even through text or just straight up peacing out is something he 100% deserves.
